prompt.alinti: This GitHub repo just hit number one trending in the world because it fixes the most expensive and unproductive habit in all of AI, vibe coding.
Vibe coding is a complete waste of your time.
Instead, you should be using the skills in this repo to do something called agentic engineering.
Vibe coding is just prompting and hoping for the best.
Super quick to get started, but before you know it, you're stuck, things are breaking, you're going in circles, and you have no idea how you got there or what to do to fix it.
Agentic engineering, on the other hand, is a more structured process where you remain in control at every step of the process.
You're using AI to plan your work, break it down into smaller chunks, and then you're using agents to test what you've created at each step of the process.
This repo lets you start doing that in five simple steps with a set of skills.
Number one is grill meat. Agents will interview you relentlessly until your plan for what you want to build is absolutely crystal clear.
Number two is specs. The agent turns your conversation into a written spec that outlines exactly what's going to be built in plain English.
Number three is tickets. AI breaks that spec down into smaller chunks with technical instructions that AI can then go and implement.
Number four is build. Each ticket is implemented by a new agent with a fresh context window.
And the fifth and last step is a review. The code is checked. Does it pass all your tests? And does it actually match what you had in the spec at the beginning?

And from there, you remain in control. If you need to iterate, don't go in and blindly change the code. All you need to do is change the spec that's written in plain English and then the agent will change the code for you.
Comment 'AGENTIC' below and I'll send you the repo and some tutorials from the creator of this repo, Matt Pocock, who's an absolute legend.
